newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia Silver Swan nickel mine gears for start.
newsitem.headline: Australia Silver Swan nickel mine gears for start.

text.p: Production from the A$46 million Silver Swan nickel mine in Western Australia is scheduled to start next month, project operator Mining Project Investors Pty Ltd (MPI) said on Thursday.
Silver Swan is the first of a string of new nickel projects to be developed under Western Australia's so-called "nickel boom", centered on the normally gold-obsessed eastern goldfields region.

The mine is slated to produce about 29,000 tonnes of nickel concentrate annually, all of which is earmarked for the Harjavalta nickel smelter in Finland, owned by Outokumpu Oy a 50/50 partner with MPI in the project, Graham Brock, project manager of MPI told Reuters.
"Everything so far is good," Brock said.
The Harjavalta smelter is already being supplied by Outokumpu's Forrestania nickel mine in Western Australia, he said.
Outokumpu is traded on the Helsinki Stock Exchange. MPI is privately held.

The Silver Swan discovery was made in November 1995 by MPI and Outokumpu, 45 km north east of Kalgoorlie, surprising much of the town's mining establishment and sending stock prices of neighbouring mining companies soaring.
Joseph Gutnick's Mt Kersey Mines NL Australian Diamond Exploration NL and Ashton Mining Ltd were among the beneficiaries.
Silver Swan, a high grade deposit contained within the Balck Swan mineral deposit, is the first of a handful of nickel projects in Western Australia expected to reach the production phase.

Other hopefuls in the region include Anaconda Nickel Ltd's Murrin Murin project, the Lake Johnston/Maggie hays project being developed by Forrestania Gold NL with technical help from Gencor Ltd of South Africa.
Resolute Ltd is developing the Bulong nickel mine, while Dominion Mining Ltd has expressed confidence its Yakabindie mine will be developed.

Demand from nickel is forecast by analysts to remain firm at least over the next few years, given bright prospects for world consumption of stainless steel. Nickel is widely used as an alloy in most forms of stainless steel.
